## e5030f1df7fa

**A2 — Reproduced distribution/teaching defect: touching rings are absent from generation.** Findings-only audit; the generator and reference rule remain unchanged. No incorrect Racket label was observed in the focused check below.

**Source identity.** Generator version `2.2.0`, SHA-256 `87f5e3a0fbea51a32f498fbbd3748101b7cb3c700c79c98c45af65e6f114ce0d`; selected/executed rule hash `43f5e4f328ce`; exact rule-text SHA-256 `05c1ed50bf029c8a73d22654e8e9a1a1a8bb21defca8e54bd0a790f52eb5bc7e`. All counts below use these unchanged audit-source bytes.

The canonical rule fills every exact hollow yellow 3×3 window, including windows in a larger connected yellow shape. Canonical variant 0, training pair index 2 contains two edge-touching rings. The generator's `_free(..., halo=1)` and `_place` prevent rings from touching any previously placed nonzero cell; its normal inputs therefore make each yellow ring an isolated eight-cell component. Its other yellow shapes are a solid 3×3 square, a 2×2 square, lines, or an L. This allows the simpler rule **“fill only yellow 4-connected components that are exactly one eight-cell 3×3 ring”** to agree throughout this isolated-ring support while failing a canonical case.

**Concrete witness.** [witness.json](checks/audit/e5030f1df7fa/witness.json) retains the exact canonical input, actual Racket output, rival output, source hashes and command. This is a **canonical witness**, not a generated sample or a validator-only construction. It passes `self_check` with `[]` and belongs to the canonical task domain, while falling outside the generator's documented isolated-ring restriction. At zero-based `(row, column)` coordinates `(1, 5)` and `(2, 8)`, Racket outputs red `2` and the component rival leaves background `0`. Both windows must be filled even though their yellow outlines connect.

**Measured check.** The supported `arcpuzzles apply` command labelled all five usable canonical pairs and 24 generated cases: seeds **0–7**, sample index **0**, each of **easy / medium / hard**, overrides **`{}`**. The 24 generated cases contain **23 unique input grids**. All **24/24** generated cases and **5/5** canonical inputs passed `self_check`. Racket matched canonical labels **5/5**; the component rival matched Racket on **24/24** generated cases and **4/5** canonical pairs. The sole canonical failure is retained above. These are individual-grid measurements, not a lesson-identifiability or query-rotation census. No `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS` or `LESSON_COMPETITORS` declaration exists in this source, and the rival is not claimed to fit every canonical pair.

**Implication and proposed repair.** Include edge-touching yellow rings as an ordinary generation axis and add a focused canonical regression. A teaching policy should place a touching-ring witness in the demonstrations when it intends to refute component-based matching. Correct labels on the current isolated examples cannot distinguish these two rules. This audit supplies evidence only; it does not change the target, claim a production/rotation lesson verdict, or run a full battery.

**Evidence and replay.** [probe.py](checks/audit/e5030f1df7fa/probe.py), [probe.json](checks/audit/e5030f1df7fa/probe.json), [input.json](checks/audit/e5030f1df7fa/input.json), [cases.json](checks/audit/e5030f1df7fa/cases.json), [racket.json](checks/audit/e5030f1df7fa/racket.json), and [verification-commands.json](checks/audit/e5030f1df7fa/verification-commands.json). Run the recorded wrapper commands from `WORK`; each payload executes from `WORK/repo`. All three verification commands exited `0`.
